channel.title: Open Origins news
channel.description: Map and test every route to the origin of life, by 2027

item.title: Critics say assembly theory reduces to dictionary compression (Ozelim, Uthamacumaran, Abrahão et al.)
item.description: The latest round of the assembly-theory dispute: critics say the 2025 defence used incomplete controls.

item.title: Lipid membranes made from scratch without an existing membrane (Khanal, Fracassi, Harjung, Burkart, Devaraj)
item.description: Vesicles assembled from lipids built out of acetate and cysteine, with no pre-existing membrane to grow from.

item.title: All five nucleobases found in asteroid Ryugu (Koga, Oba, Takano, Naraoka et al.)
item.description: Ryugu, like Bennu, holds all five letters used in DNA and RNA.

item.title: A small polymerase ribozyme that can synthesize itself and its complementary strand (Gianni, Holliger et al.)
item.description: A 45-letter RNA, QT45, found in random sequences, copies RNA in ice and made both a copy of itself and of its partner strand.

item.title: Bio-essential sugars, including ribose, in samples from asteroid Bennu (Furukawa et al.)
item.description: Ribose, the sugar in RNA, and glucose found in Bennu; deoxyribose, the DNA sugar, was not.

item.title: Thioester-mediated RNA aminoacylation and peptidyl-RNA synthesis in water (Singh, Powner et al.)
item.description: Amino acids carried on sulfur compounds attach to the ends of RNA in water, ahead of joining to each other.

item.title: Insufficient evidence for DMS and DMDS in the atmosphere of K2-18 b (Luque et al.)
item.description: No statistically significant detection of DMS or DMDS when all JWST data on K2-18 b are analysed together.

item.title: Carbon reduction powered by natural electrochemical gradients under vent conditions (Altair et al.)
item.description: A vent-wall reactor makes formic and acetic acid from CO2 and H2 using only pH gradients across iron-sulfide minerals.

item.title: High-yield polymerisation of cyclic nucleotides under wet-dry cycling (Caimi, Braun, Fraccia et al.)
item.description: Repeated drying and wetting joins all four RNA letters into short chains, with no added activating chemicals.

item.title: Triplet substrates under pH and freeze-thaw cycles enable exponential RNA replication by a ribozyme (Attwater, Holliger et al.)
item.description: An RNA enzyme replicated both strands of short double-stranded RNAs exponentially, including a piece of itself.

item.title: Abundant ammonia and nitrogen-rich organic matter in asteroid Bennu (Glavin, Dworkin et al.)
item.description: 33 amino acids, 14 of the 20 used by life, and all five nucleobases in pristine Bennu samples; the chiral amino acids show no handedness bias.

item.title: The nature of the last universal common ancestor and its impact on the early Earth system (Moody et al.)
item.description: Places LUCA about 4.2 billion years ago as a complex anaerobic acetogen living within an ecosystem.

item.title: Heat flows enrich prebiotic building blocks and enhance their reactivity (Matreux, Aikkila, Scheu, Braun, Mast)
item.description: Heat flowing through rock cracks sorts a mixed prebiotic soup, doing the purification chemists normally do by hand.

item.title: RNA-catalysed evolution of catalytic RNA (Papastavrou, Horning, Joyce)
item.description: An RNA polymerase ribozyme, not a protein, ran Darwinian evolution of another ribozyme, but only when its copying was accurate enough.

item.title: Molecular assembly indices of mineral heteropolyanions (Hazen et al.)
item.description: Some mineral building units score above the assembly-index threshold proposed for life.

item.title: The physiology and habitat of the last universal common ancestor (Weiss et al.)
item.description: 355 protein families point to a LUCA that lived on hydrogen, CO2 and iron, probably at a hydrothermal setting.

item.title: Synthesis of activated pyrimidine ribonucleotides in prebiotically plausible conditions (Powner, Gerland, Sutherland)
item.description: RNA's C and U building blocks made by a route that skips free ribose and free bases, the step that had blocked RNA-world chemistry.

item.title: From ligase to polymerase: the class I ribozyme lineage (Bartel, Joyce and co-workers)
item.description: Twenty years of lab evolution turned an RNA that joins RNA into one that copies long RNAs, but not well enough to copy itself.

item.title: A production of amino acids under possible primitive Earth conditions (Miller)
item.description: Electric sparks through a mix of methane, ammonia, hydrogen and water made amino acids.
